approved: Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2014 Measures No. 2) Bill 2014

Moved an amendment condemning the government's GP tax and health cuts, citing New South Wales Treasurer Andrew Constance's warning of a loss of more than $1 billion over the forward estimates for hospital services, and noting the budget cuts more than $80 billion from health and education combined, including $368 million from the National Partnership on Preventive Health.

Detailed the GP tax's local impact in her Parramatta electorate, which had a 95.3 per cent bulk-billing rate, meaning the tax would have cost the community $9.1 million based on last year's bulk-billed visits, on top of $100 million already cut from Westmead Hospital.

Supported the Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment Bill, which clears a backlog of 96 unlegislated tax measures inherited from Labor, including scrapping a proposed $1.8 billion fringe benefits tax change on car leasing, and said closing a 'distribution washing' loophole would raise $60 million.
